claims.text: Arador succeeded his father, Argonui, when he died in .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Realms in Exile", "The Northern Line: Heirs of Isildur", Chieftains, entry for Argonui, p. 1038

claims.text: In his time many Dúnedain of the North lived in woods between the river Hoarwell and the river Loudwater. Arador lived in a house north of the Trollshaws in woods near the river Hoarwell, which was threatened by a group of Trolls.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Carl F. Hostetter (ed.), "Part Three. The World, its Lands, and its Inhabitants: XVII. Silvan Elves and Silvan Elvish", The Nature of Middle-earth, HarperCollins, 2021, note 12, p. 366

claims.text: His rule was uneventful except for the fact that he was captured by Hill-trolls in the Coldfells north of Rivendell and killed by them. He was succeeded by his young son, Arathorn II, in .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Tale of Aragorn and Arwen", p. 1057; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Realms in Exile", "The Northern Line: Heirs of Isildur", Chieftains, entry for Arathorn II, p. 1038
